help.title: Help
help.intro: Short answers to the usual questions.

share.title: Share the catalog at home
steps: On one device, open "Sharing and devices" and tap "Show code".
On the other, in the same place, scan the QR or paste the code.
Done: they sync on their own whenever they are on the same Wi-Fi.

away.title: Share away from home
steps: Turn on the hotspot ("internet sharing") on a phone.
Connect the other device to that network.
Pair or sync as at home. It uses no data: everything goes between the two devices.

pairing.title: The phone will not pair
steps: Both on the same Wi-Fi, not on mobile data. Avoid guest networks.
Keep the code on screen on the other device: it works once, for 10 minutes.
Turn off any VPN while pairing.
On Windows, allow the app on private networks when the firewall asks.
If the phone asks for "local network" or "nearby devices" permission, allow it.
If nothing works, restart the app on both and create a new code.

backups.title: Backups
steps: In "Backups", "Save backup" creates a file with everything, covers included. It is protected with a password by default.
Without the password nobody can open it, and the app does not keep it: write it down.
Keep the file wherever you like: a folder, Google Drive, a USB stick.
To get it back, use "Restore backup" and enter the password.

lost.title: If you lose your phone
steps: What you had is still on the devices it synced with, and in your backups.
On another device, open "Sharing and devices" and forget the lost one.
On the new phone, install the app and pair again.

search.title: Look up a book's details
steps: When adding, type or scan the ISBN and tap "Search": details come from Open Library and Google Books.
Offline, you can add it by hand and complete it later.
Google Books works better with your own key, set in Settings.

codeExpired.help: Codes last 15 minutes. Ask for a new one and use it as soon as it arrives.

tooManyAttempts.title: Too many attempts with this code.
tooManyAttempts.help: It no longer works. Ask for a new one; it arrives in a moment.

registrationClosed.title: This server is not taking new accounts for now.
registrationClosed.help: If you already have an account, sign in. If you expected to be able to create one, talk to whoever runs the server.

invalidCredentials.title: The email or password is incorrect.
invalidCredentials.help: Check how the email is spelled. If you don't remember your password, set a new one.

accountNotConfirmed.title: Your email isn't confirmed yet.
accountNotConfirmed.help: We sent you a code when you created the account. If you can't find it, ask for another.

accountBlocked.title: This account is locked.
accountBlocked.help: If you think this is a mistake, contact whoever runs the server.

invalidTotp.title: That code isn't right.
invalidTotp.help: Use the one showing now in the app; it changes every 30 seconds. Make sure your phone sets the time automatically.

invalidBackupCode.title: That backup code doesn't work.
invalidBackupCode.help: You may have used it already; each one works once. Try another from your list.

serverUnavailable.title: The server isn't responding.
serverUnavailable.help: It may be under maintenance, or the address is wrong. Try again in a few minutes.

passwordShort.title: Your password needs at least 8 characters.

invalidInput.title: This information isn't valid.
invalidInput.help: Check the fields and try again.

invalidServer.title: This address isn't valid.
invalidServer.help: Check that it's a Kosmotheka server's address.

deviceRemoved.title: This device was removed from an account.

signedOut.title: You've been signed out.
signedOut.help: Your password was changed on another device.

twoFactorUnavailable.title: The second factor isn't available on this server.
twoFactorUnavailable.help: It may have been turned off since you opened this screen. Try again later.

twoFactorAlreadyEnabled.title: The second factor was already on.
twoFactorAlreadyEnabled.help: Reload the account screen to see its current state.

twoFactorNotStarted.title: There's no setup in progress.
twoFactorNotStarted.help: Go back to "Turn on" to get a new code.

twoFactorNotEnabled.title: The second factor isn't on.
twoFactorNotEnabled.help: Reload the account screen to see its current state.

notFound.title: Something went wrong.
notFound.help: Try again. If it keeps happening, report it.

invalidRequest.title: Something went wrong.
invalidRequest.help: Try again. If it keeps happening, report it.

schemaVersion.title: This app version cannot sync with the server.
schemaVersion.help: Update the app and try again.

deviceAlreadyReset.title: Too late: that device already connected and was wiped.
deviceAlreadyReset.help: It can't be undone once the device has connected.

noPassword.title: This account has no password.
noPassword.help: You signed in with Google: no password is used here.

deviceTaken.title: This device is signed in to another account.
deviceTaken.help: To use it with this one, first leave it to another person in Settings › This device: it starts afresh, as if just installed.

deviceKeyMismatch.title: Your account knows this device with another key.
deviceKeyMismatch.help: Remove it from your account on another device, in Account › My devices, and sign in here again.

linkRejected.title: The cloud did not accept this library’s link.
linkRejected.help: Nothing was uploaded. Try again; if it repeats, tell whoever administers the library.

linkNotAllowed.title: Only whoever administers this library can upload it.
linkNotAllowed.help: Meanwhile, it keeps sharing over your home network.

eventsUnavailable.title: This server does not send live updates.
eventsUnavailable.help: Changes arrive when the app syncs.

accessWithdrawn.title: The cloud says you no longer have access to this library.

people.revokeBody: The link or email stops working. {{person}} stays in the library and you can invite them again.

invite.title: Invite to “{{library}}”
invite.description: Invite someone to “{{library}}”, by email or with a link to copy.

email.label: By email
email.hint: They get a link by email. Only that email address can use it.

link.label: Copy link
link.hint: Whoever opens it first gets in. Give it only to that person.

invite.name: Name
invite.nameHint: This is how they will appear in People until they get in.
invite.emailHint: Only used to send the invitation. It is not kept.
invite.existingBody: {{person}} is already in the library. They will get a link by email to sign in and use their own account.
invite.keepsRole: {{person}} keeps their role. The link only connects their account.
invite.readerNote: They get in as a reader; you can change their role here afterwards.
invite.useQr: They are here: use the QR instead
invite.copyFailed: The link could not be copied. Select it and copy it by hand.

not_signed_in.body: To invite you need to be signed in to your account.

not_in_cloud.body: “{{library}}” is not in the cloud yet. Upload it first and then you can invite.

no_roles.body: “{{library}}” has no people with roles yet. Turn them on first, so each invitation has someone to be for.

no_cloud_power.body: The cloud is not allowed to give access to new devices in “{{library}}”. Turn that on in the library’s settings.

server_without_invitations.body: This server does not make invitations. You can still give access with the QR.

result.createdButFailed: We added {{person}} to the library, but the invitation could not be created.
result.failed: The invitation could not be created.
result.retryByEmail: You can try again by email from {{person}}’s page.
result.readerOnly: {{person}} gets in as a reader. You can change that in People.
result.closeWarning: If you close this you will not be able to see the link again. If you did not copy it, cancel the invitation in People and make another.

open.entryHint: Paste a link someone sent you
open.title: I have an invitation
open.description: Paste an invitation link to join a library.
open.expired: The invitation to “{{library}}” expired while you were signing in. Ask for a new one and paste it here.
open.placeholder: Paste the link you were sent here
open.hint: Paste the link you were sent. Nothing happens until you say so.
open.signedInBody: You will join “{{library}}” with the account {{account}}.
open.signInFirst: Sign in or create an account to get in.
open.joinedLater: You are in. The library will arrive in a moment, the next time the app syncs.

errors.unknown: The invitation could not be completed. Try again.
errors.invitations_unavailable: This server does not make invitations.
errors.invitation_forbidden: Only whoever administers the library can invite.
errors.invitation_library_not_ready: This library cannot invite yet: it needs people with roles and the cloud allowed to link devices.
errors.invitation_person_unsuitable: That person cannot be invited now.
errors.invitation_expired: It has expired: ask whoever administers for a new one.
errors.invitation_not_for_this_account: This invitation is for another account.
errors.invitation_account_already_in_library: Your account is already another person in this library.
errors.too_many_requests: Too many attempts. Wait a little and try again.
errors.not_signed_in: Sign in to your account first.
errors.not_in_cloud: This library is not in your cloud account.
errors.no_roles: This library has no people with roles yet, so there is nobody to link an account to.
errors.no_cloud_power: The cloud is not allowed to link new devices in this library. Turn it on in the library’s settings.
errors.server_without_invitations: This server does not make invitations.
errors.invalid_email: That email address does not look right.
errors.link_needs_new_person: A link is only for somebody new. For someone already in the library, use their email.
errors.person_not_invitable: That person cannot be invited: they administer the library, have no access, or already have an account.
errors.invitation_bad_link: That is not an invitation link.
errors.invitation_other_server: This link belongs to another server than your account’s. It was not opened.
errors.server_unavailable: The server cannot be reached. Check your connection and try again.
errors.invitation_other_account: This invitation was opened with another account. Open the link again.

errors.unknown: Something went wrong with the cloud. Try again.
errors.not_found: That library is not in your cloud account any more.
errors.schema_version: The app and the server run different versions. Update the app.
errors.not_signed_in: Sign in to your account to use the cloud.
errors.unsigned_history: This library has changes from before signing existed, so it cannot go to the cloud. Duplicate it as a new library and upload that one.
errors.already_linked: This library is already in a cloud.
errors.link_rejected: The cloud did not accept this library’s link. Nothing was uploaded; try again.
errors.link_not_allowed: Only whoever administers this library can upload it. Meanwhile, it keeps sharing over your home network.
errors.events_unavailable: This server does not send live updates: changes arrive when the app syncs.
errors.access_withdrawn: The cloud says you no longer have access to this library.
errors.no_cloud_device: This server cannot give the cloud that power in this library.

autolink.label: The cloud can give access to new devices
autolink.on: On: a new phone belonging to someone at home with an account gets in on its own, with that person’s role.
autolink.off: Off: whoever manages the library links each new device by hand, as without the cloud.
autolink.offBody: Devices already in the library stay as they are. You will have to link new ones by hand, even if their person has an account.
autolink.pickLabel: The cloud can give access to my new devices
autolink.pickHint: A new phone belonging to someone at home with an account gets in on its own, with that person’s role. You can change this in each library’s settings.

otherOwner.title: In “{{library}}”, this device belongs to {{person}}
otherOwner.body: You signed in with your account, but whoever administers the library said this device belongs to someone else.
otherOwner.keep: It stays as it is: in “{{library}}” you see the library as {{as}}.
otherOwner.change: To change whose it is, whoever administers the library has to do it from their own device, in People.
otherOwner.foot: We will not ask again on this device, unless another account signs in or the device changes hands.

download.title: Downloading your libraries from the cloud
download.lead: Large libraries can take a while. Nobody at home needs to do anything.

notice.joinedOne: You are now in “{{name}}” in the cloud. As {{as}}.
notice.joinedMany_one: You are now in {{count}} library in the cloud · {{list}}
notice.joinedMany_other: You are now in {{count}} libraries in the cloud · {{list}}
notice.downloadedCount_one: {{count}} library came down from your cloud.
notice.downloadedCount_other: {{count}} libraries came down from your cloud.
notice.downloadedNotUploaded: Libraries you did not upload are still on your other devices.
notice.libraryConflict: «{{name}}» was not brought down from the cloud: this device already has a different library that the app identifies the same way. Nothing was mixed.
notice.missingInCloud: {{name}} is no longer in your cloud account. It stays on this device.
notice.deletedHere: You deleted a library on this device that is still in your cloud. It was not downloaded again.
notice.removed: You are no longer in “{{name}}”. Whoever administers it withdrew your access, and the library was deleted from this device. If you think it is a mistake, talk to whoever administers it; to come back, ask them to link this device again.
notice.accessWithdrawn: “{{name}}” stopped syncing with the cloud. The cloud says you no longer have access, but this device could not confirm it. The library stays here and on your home network. Talk to whoever administers it.
notice.notLinked: The cloud offered a library that was not properly linked. It was ignored.
notice.failed: “{{name}}” could not be synced with the cloud this time. The other libraries were. It will be tried again.

pick.title: Which libraries do you want in the cloud?
pick.lead: The ones you do not upload keep working as before, over your home network.
pick.signedOut: Sign in to your account to take libraries to the cloud.
pick.otherServer: In a cloud on another server
pick.unsigned: It has changes from before signing existed, so it cannot go up as it is. A copy can.
pick.duplicated: Created “{{name}}”. It is ticked, so you can upload it now.
pick.duplicateFailed: The copy could not be made. Nothing changed.
pick.later: You can upload more later, from the library or from your account.
pick.done_one: {{count}} library is now in the cloud.
pick.done_other: {{count}} libraries are now in the cloud.

row.missing: No longer in your cloud account
row.otherServer: In a cloud on another server
row.conflict: Not mixed with another library on this device
row.unsigned: Needs a copy to go up
row.locked: Only whoever administers it can upload it

sharing.title: Cloud
sharing.hint: Your account keeps a copy, so your devices sync from anywhere.
sharing.offlineHelp: Everything still works here and on your home network; changes will upload once you are back online.

scanner.notIsbn: That was a shop label, not the ISBN. Type the small number that starts with 978 or 979, or scan again aiming at its code.
scanner.qrHint: Point at the code on the other device

local.title: Your library, on your device
local.body: Kosmotheka keeps your catalog on this device. It works without an account or a connection, and your data stays here unless you ask otherwise.

scan.title: Scan the barcode
scan.body: Use the camera to add a book in a moment or to check whether you already have it, say in a bookshop. On books, look for the code that starts with 978 or 979.

search.title: Public catalogs to fill in the details
search.body: To fill in a work's details, the app asks these public catalogs. Only what you search for is sent (an ISBN, a code or a title), never your catalog or your data. Turn off any you like.
search.later: You can change this any time in Settings → Data providers. Without them, everything can be added by hand.

share.title: Share it if you like
share.body: You can pair other devices at home over the local network, or create an account to sync through the cloud. It's optional: it's in the menu whenever you want it.
